extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in wartime news
extracted.subtask_description: Writing newspaper news stories that report military operations and wartime events, using datelines, official communiqués, tactical specifics, and human-interest vignettes for a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire-service attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a clear dateline and attribution to the reporting service (e.g., 'Allied Headquarters in North Africa, April 9 (A. P.).').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead with location and date and show the wire service or correspondent source so readers know where and by whom the report is filed. Examples in the text: multiple datelines followed by '(A. P.)' or 'By the Associated Press.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Source attribution to official communiqués and broadcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute operational claims and casualty/equipment figures to named official sources (communiqués, military quarters, Air Ministry, radio broadcasts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting numbers or battlefield claims, specify the origin — e.g., 'a communique announced', 'military quarters said', 'a British broadcast recorded here by the Columbia listening post', or 'the Air Ministry said tonight.' Make clear whether the statement is from an official communique, broadcast, or unnamed military quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative specifics (numbers and distances)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide concrete numerical details such as prisoner counts, vehicles destroyed/damaged, distances, miles advanced, and losses (e.g., 'taken 9,500 prisoners', '130 enemy vehicles had been destroyed and 200 damaged').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise figures and distances to convey scale and progress. Include units and context (e.g., miles from key ports, number of prisoners since a given date). Note uncertainties or sourcing if figures are provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-domain operational coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Cover land, air, and naval actions rather than focusing on a single domain (e.g., armored advances, fighter-bomber strikes, naval motor craft night attack off Bizerte).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe operations across domains to give a full picture of the campaign: armored vanguards, aerial assaults, naval engagements. Include the interactions between domains (air strikes enabling ground pursuit, naval interdiction of convoys).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic context and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the broader strategic consequences of tactical developments (e.g., junction of forces will relieve shipping and shorten supply lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place battlefield events into larger strategic terms so readers understand significance: effects on supply routes, potential for encirclement, impact on future operations. Use quotes from commanders or analysis to support the context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of named commanders, units and place names
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify commanders, army corps, divisions, unit designations and specific geographic locations (e.g., Gen. Sir Harold L. Alexander, Lieut.-Gen. Kenneth A. N. Anderson, Wadi el Akarit, Mahares, Mezzouna).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate unit and place names to anchor the story. Spell out ranks/titles and relation to the action; give proximity (miles) to major landmarks or ports when relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-interest vignettes and firsthand anecdote
rubrics_metrics.description: Include short, vivid human-interest stories or soldier anecdotes to humanize the campaign (e.g., Italian tries to surrender; Yank too sleepy to bother; stories of exhausted infantrymen holding a hill).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interleave operational reporting with personal anecdotes, named individuals, and direct-reported dialogue to provide emotional texture and reader engagement. Keep such anecdotes brief and clearly identified as firsthand or delayed field accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of vivid sensory description for combat scenes
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ descriptive language to convey battlefield sights and sounds (e.g., 'huge barrage shattered the quiet', 'flashes gashed the sky', 'tracer bullets cut across the horizon').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appropriate, use sensory details to illustrate intensity and atmosphere of combat, while retaining factual clarity. Balance evocative prose with accuracy and attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headlines and subheads to structure coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Use bold headlines and subheads to summarize main developments and break the story into topical segments (e.g., 'AMERICAN PLANES HURRY ROMMEL'S RETREAT', 'NAZIS FLEE IN ROUT').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft headlines that emphasize the principal action or significance; employ subheads for secondary items. Ensure subheads reflect content that follows and do not overclaim beyond sourced facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological and geographic sequencing
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize narrative with a clear sequence of events and geographically specific movements (pursuits, withdrawals, where junctions are expected to occur).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrange paragraphs so readers can follow time and movement: where forces were, where they moved, and where contact occurred. Use distances and directional cues (north, northeast, toward the coast) to orient the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution of uncertainty and reporting limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge when information is uncertain, when results cannot be fully ascertained, or when weather hampered observation (e.g., 'it was not ascertained how many tanks were knocked out', 'weather prevented full observance of results').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit about limits to verification: report that numbers or effects are provisional, that weather prevented assessment, or that enemy broadcasts offer partisan claims. Avoid presenting unverified claims as fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combining operational reporting with material/equipment impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Pair accounts of maneuvers with effects on materiel and logistics (e.g., transport destruction, shortages of motor transports, ships sunk by bombers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how operations affect equipment and supply lines: vehicles destroyed/damaged, ships sunk, airfields hit, and resulting shortages. This helps readers understand operational sustainability and consequences.
